gloss: good or bad; merits and demerits

definitions.gloss: good or bad; right or wrong; merits and demerits; quality
definitions.explanation: The relative merit or quality of something, encompassing both its good and bad aspects. Used when evaluating or judging something from multiple angles.

examples.japanese: {善|よ}し{悪|あ}しは{別|べつ}として、{決|き}まったことだ。
examples.english: Regardless of whether it's good or bad, it's been decided.

examples.japanese: この{方法|ほうほう}の{善|よ}し{悪|あ}しを{検討|けんとう}する{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: We need to examine the merits and demerits of this method.

examples.japanese: {物事|ものごと}の{善|よ}し{悪|あ}しを{判断|はんだん}できる{年齢|ねんれい}になった。
examples.english: He has reached an age where he can judge right from wrong.

notes:
USAGE:
Commonly used when evaluating something without committing to a judgment: {善|よ}し{悪|あ}しは{別|べつ}として (setting aside whether it's good or bad). Also used to talk about the quality of results or outcomes.

WRITING:
Also written as {良|よ}し{悪|あ}し. Both spellings are common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {善|よ}し{悪|あ}しは{別|べつ}として (regardless of merits)
- {善|よ}し{悪|あ}しを{判断|はんだん}する (to judge good and bad)
- {善|よ}し{悪|あ}しがある (to have pros and cons)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {良|りょう}{否|ひ}: pass or fail — more formal, used for evaluation outcomes
- {是非|ぜひ}: right and wrong — more formal; also commonly used as an adverb meaning "by all means"
